calls.body: The Blue Jackets played last night and get no rest before this one. Teams in that spot usually get the worse of the chances, so we expect the Wild to control more of the play than they usually do.

calls.head: The Blue Jackets’ defense joins the attack, the Wild’s stays home
calls.body: The Blue Jackets’ defensemen shoot a lot, and the Wild’s not so much. Columbus is one of the league’s best for shots from defensemen, and Minnesota is the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Watch the Blue Jackets’ defensemen jump into the play.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Wild beat the Blue Jackets
paras: Danila Yurov opened the scoring for the Wild late in the first. Adam Fantilli tied it 1-1 for Columbus a minute later, but the Blue Jackets didn’t score again. Kirill Kaprizov put the Wild ahead for good on the power play early in the second, with Joel Eriksson Ek picking up his 200th NHL assist on the goal.

The Wild earned this one. Replay the chances a hundred times and they win about seven in ten. Jesper Wallstedt needed only 13 saves for the Wild, and Cam Talbot, who gave up six goals against Florida in his last start, kept the Blue Jackets in it, stopping 32 of 34.

The Blue Jackets killed off a two-man advantage that lasted just under two minutes early in the first. The Wild improved to 6-2-1 and climbed into first in the Central, while the Jackets fell to 3-4-0, seventh in the Metropolitan.

items.text: Kirill Kaprizov has a point in six straight games, with a goal in each of the last three.

The Wild won without Jared Spurgeon, Marcus Foligno, Olli Määttä and others. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Flyers were missing more at the time.
Quinn Hughes’s eight-game point streak ended.
Two of the preview’s three calls held.
